description: Grade 5 example: name an interval under a key signature (G major, treble clef).

provenance.authoredBy: Music Theory Path curriculum team (Brief 10 addendum)

item.prompt: The key signature of G major is shown. Name the interval between these two notes (number and quality).

music.textAlternative: Two notes in G major (one sharp, F♯): B4 and F♮5. The natural sign overrides the key signature. Both notes are minims.

hints: Apply the key signature to both notes before you count.
Count the letter names for the number, then compare with the major scale on the lower note for the quality.

feedback.correct: Correct. The natural sign cancels the key signature's F♯ for this note, so the top note is F♮. B to F♮ is a diminished 5th; B to F♯ would be perfect.

mistakes.accidental-not-applied: Look at the sign beside the note. The natural sign cancels the key signature's F♯ for this note, so the top note is F♮. B to F♮ is a diminished 5th; B to F♯ would be perfect.
mistakes.counted-one-end-only: Count both notes: the lower note is 1, then every letter name up to and including the upper note.
mistakes.quality-from-wrong-key: Judge the quality against the major scale of the lower note, using the sharps or flats actually sounding.

feedback.fallback: The answer is a diminished 5. The natural sign cancels the key signature's F♯ for this note, so the top note is F♮. B to F♮ is a diminished 5th; B to F♯ would be perfect.
